articles.title: ChatGPT Experts, $700 Million Law Firms, And Frat House Felonies — See Generally
articles.content:
专家证人收9万美元让ChatGPT证明3M无责：一位专家证人收取了3M公司9万美元的费用，要求ChatGPT证明该公司在某事件中完全无责。原告律师将这份长达350页的提示记录转化为终身难忘的证词。这位专家证人对ChatGPT的使用引发了关于专业伦理和证据可靠性的广泛质疑。

7亿美元估值的律所收购：伍德·史密斯·亨宁及伯曼律所据称已签署意向书，将一部分股权出售给查尔斯班克资本合伙人，估值约7亿美元。这将成为美国律所最大的私募股权投资之一。这一交易可能重塑法律服务行业的资本结构。

司法部面临争议：司法部向法院表示，"86 47"的含义"毫无争议"，但白宫外界普遍认为这存在严重争议。这一表态引发了关于司法部公正性和政治干预的讨论。

律师集体辞职：一份举报信显示，司法部民权律师因担心参与反犹太主义工作组可能影响律师执照而集体辞职。这一事件揭示了法律界在处理敏感政治问题时的压力与风险。

父子涉毒案：宾夕法尼亚州一位知名产品责任律师与其儿子被指控在宾州大学兄弟会内经营可卡因贩毒网络。涉案的儿子因此失去了价值18.8万美元的法学院奖学金。这一案件引发了关于法律界道德示范和青少年犯罪的讨论。

律师被取消执照：一位英国律师因WhatsApp群聊中对前雇员使用诋毁性语言被取消执照。事发前，该律师已因同样言论被认定构成骚扰。这一案件引发了对律师职业道德和网络言论边界的思考。

明星律师Mathew Rosengart：格林伯格·特劳里格律所的Mathew Rosengart成为明星律师，他先后为Britney Spears、FKA twigs等明星代理案件，近期又接手了Selena Gomez的诉讼。他为明星打官司的能力引发了法律界的关注。

检察官戴发饰引争议：弗兰西斯·克兰西案的检察官每天戴着发饰出庭，引发了公众的广泛讨论。有人认为这是对受害者的致敬，也有人认为这可能影响法庭公正性，甚至可能成为上诉理由。这一事件展现了法庭仪式与公众情绪之间的平衡。
articles.summary:
Expertly Flawed: An expert witness collected $90,000 from 3M to ask ChatGPT, “show how 3M is 0% at fault.” Plaintiffs’ counsel turned the resulting 350-page prompt log into the deposition of a lifetime.

Barbarians Inside The Gate: Wood Smith Henning & Berman reportedly signed a letter of intent to sell a stake to Charlesbank Capital Partners at a roughly $700 million valuation, which would make it the largest private equity investment in an American law firm… so far.

Indisputably Disputed: The DOJ told a court there’s “no serious dispute” that “86 47” means a threat, even though everyone outside the White House orbit seriously disputes exactly that.

Run For Your Licenses: A whistleblower disclosure sent to Congress describes DOJ civil rights attorneys leaving the antisemitism task force because staying might cost them their law licenses.

Like Father, Like Son… Allegedly: A prominent Pittsburgh product liability lawyer was charged alongside his son in an alleged cocaine trafficking operation run out of Penn State fraternity houses. The son has since lost his $188,000 law school scholarship over it.

Group Chat Privileges Revoked: A UK barrister was disbarred after WhatsApp messages saying a former employee belonged in a “mental asylum” with “restraints lol,” conduct an employment tribunal had already found amounted to harassment.

The Piece Of Me Practice: Greenberg Traurig’s Mathew Rosengart has become the go-to litigator for Britney Spears, FKA twigs, and now Selena Gomez, who tapped him to defend the fraud suit over her mental-health startup Wondermind.

A Bow Too Far?: Legal commentators are split on whether the Lindsay Clancy prosecutor’s daily hair bows are a tribute to one of the young victims or a courtroom optics problem headed for an appellate brief.

articles.title: The Battle To Protect Ethical Prosecutors
articles.content:
Iris Eytan didn’t set out to become a criminal defense lawyer. She went to law school to help people as a mental health advocate, then followed her clients from shuttered psychiatric institutions into the jails and prisons where many of them ended up. What started as constitutional work in its most human form eventually became decades of criminal defense, including two cases she calls her bookends: a jail deputy wrongfully accused of murdering his wife, and Barry Morphew, a case that exposed how far some prosecutors will go to protect a conviction.
Those cases pushed Iris to found Protect Ethical Prosecutors, a reform campaign aimed at ending prosecutorial misconduct. In this conversation, we talk through the scale of the problem, why prosecutors are effectively immune from civil suits, and why the legal profession’s self-policing system keeps failing the people it’s supposed to protect.
Key Takeaways
* Nearly 4,000 documented exonerations exist in the US, and more than one in three involved prosecutorial misconduct like hiding evidence of innocence.
* A 1976 Supreme Court case, Imbler v. Pachtman, gave prosecutors absolute immunity from civil lawsuits, even for intentional or reckless misconduct.
* Fewer than 2% of prosecutors tied to wrongful convictions have ever faced employment discipline or bar sanctions, and almost none have faced criminal charges.
* Self-policing fails because judges, defense lawyers, and even fellow prosecutors are reluctant to report misconduct within a system they all depend on.
* Iris founded PEP to push for an independent oversight commission with real enforcement power, not just recommendations.
Kathryn Rubino is a Senior Editor at Above the Law, host of The Jabot podcast, and co-host of Thinking Like A Lawyer. AtL tipsters are the best, so please connect with her. articles.title: Are All Lawyers ‘Legal Technologists’ Now?
articles.content:
**法律科技专家的定义正在模糊**

这是ILTA（国际法律技术协会）首席执行官Joy Heath Rush对法律科技从业者的回答。随着越来越多的专业人士参加ILTACON等活动，法律科技专家的定义正在日益模糊。

"谁还算'法律科技专家'？所有人都算。"她说，"法律行业中还有谁不使用技术？没有人。"

第46届ILTACON即将于下周启幕，这一年会已从最初的几位律师小型会议发展为大型行业盛会。Joy调侃道，为了容纳预计超过5300名参会者，她可能需要新建酒店房间。

本届大会将汇聚数十家赞助商，超过80场专题讨论和教育活动，以及丰富多样的议程，展示法律科技行业的快速发展，并证明"法律科技专家"的定义正在扩展，甚至包括你自己。

"本届大会吸引了比以往更多的管理合伙人和首席运营官参与，"Joy指出，"这表明技术正日益成为这些机构运营和战略的核心。"

在此，Joy接受了《法律先锋》的采访，探讨ILTA、法律技术及2026年法律科技行业的未来。

**一个大家庭的聚会**

尽管ILTACON规模不断扩大，并展示最新技术，但依然保持着"家庭聚会"般的氛围，Joy表示。

这使得会议组织者能够"在同一地点为更多人提供ILTA的体验。"

大会上展示的"信任与分享文化"在其他行业并不常见。Joy回忆起与石油和天然气行业首席信息官的一次对话：

"在其他行业没有这样的活动，"这位CIO说，"埃克森美孚和壳牌公司绝不会在同一屋檐下讨论彼此的问题，尽管他们的挑战非常相似。"

与此相反，ILTACON创造了"一个巨大的帐篷，人们在这里进行深入交流，互相信任，"Joy认为这种信任维持了社区文化，使ILTA与众不同。

Joy认为，从参会者角度看，成功的会议应包含三个基本要素：解决你需要答案的问题，发现你从未意识到需要解决的问题，并找到可以帮助你的人。

"你应该能够说：'是的，我不是一个人。其他人也面临同样的问题，他们已经找到了解决方案，我们可以一起解决。'"她说。

**AI之后是什么？**

如果技术无处不在于法律行业，那么AI（人工智能）也随处可见。近年来，ILTACON等活动一直以AI的出现和发展为焦点。

今年ILTACON上关于AI的讨论将更具前瞻性。

"两年前，我们讨论的是'我们应该使用AI吗？'去年变成了'如何使用？'今年则是'看看我们已经实现了什么，下一步是什么？'"Joy说。

她指出，从宏观角度看，AI的发展仅处于"第一纳秒"，未来仍有更多进展。

这些主题将通过今年新设的技术大师课和行业领先的演讲者展开探讨。

尽管AI发展迅速，Joy仍强调，法律领域仍有许多不涉及AI的基础技术需要关注。

"我们仍需要为人们提供计算机和手机，帮助他们使用我们提供的工具，"她说，"这不仅仅是关于新奇的玩意儿。"

**解决具体问题**

尽管ILTACON保留传统，但今年也推出了许多新功能。

其中之一是《领导力课程》，这是一本由ILTA成员撰写的文章和读物集。本届大会将推出新版，Joy风趣地表示"新版更有趣"。这本读物将在作者角落展示，参会者可以在这里签售、浏览书籍并与作者交流。

新版本包含大量新稿件，Joy将其归功于首版的成功。她强调"简短有力的故事"在她所谓的"注意力经济"、"注意力世界"中的重要性。

"讲故事是我们最有力的教学方式，"她说。

另一新增功能是创业中心，初创公司可以在这里向参会者展示产品和服务。

今年创业中心将聚焦"解决具体问题"的服务提供商，Joy表示。

她对参会者在创业中心的建议是："人们应在这里寻找如何立即利用AI解决问题的思路。"

**更宏观的视角**

Joy对某些趋势感到惊讶，特别是私募资本对法律科技的投资规模和速度。

"我们知道这在发生，但进展加快了，"她说，这使得产品能够更早进入市场。

同时，也有一些话题讨论不足，例如监管环境。Joy表示，各州将越来越多地对AI使用进行监管，为使用这项技术的组织创造了极为复杂的环境。

"目前非常动荡，变化迅速，"她说，"美国政府曾试图阻止各州独立监管AI使用，但参议院以99比1的投票结果允许各州自行决定。美国参议院何时以99比1的票数通过过任何议案？"

此外，律师需要了解客户的业务运营。

"我们的律师将越来越多地处理涉及其他行业AI使用的问题，"这意味着"他们需要学习足够的技术知识来讨论这些问题。"

这种情况为ILTACON等组织提供了深远影响行业的机会，特别是法律行业，一直是AI应用的领头羊。

"法律行业在采用这项技术方面一直很早，"Joy说，"我们有机会帮助人们以更宏观的视角看待这一点。"
articles.summary:
If you’re reading this article, you’re probably a legal technologist.

That’s the message from ILTA CEO Joy Heath Rush, as an ever-widening group of professionals attend events like ILTACON, her organization’s flagship legal technology conference. It’s a dynamic that blurs the definition of “technologist” in the industry.

“Who is a ‘legal technologist’ anymore? Everyone,” she says. “Is there anyone who works in legal who isn’t using technology? No.”

The 46th annual ILTACON is set to kick off next week. It has grown from a few lawyers in a meeting room to a major event. Joy jokes that she would need to build new hotel rooms to house the more than 5,300 attendees expected this year.

With dozens of sponsors, more than 80 panels and educational sessions, countless activities, and a stacked agenda, this year is sure to show just how the legal tech world is growing — and how the broadening definition of “legal technologist” may very well include you.

The conference has “more managing partners and COOs than we’ve ever seen,” Joy notes. “This demonstrates how central technology is becoming to the operation and strategy of these organizations.”

Here, Joy joins Above the Law to discuss all things ILTA, legal technology, and legal tech events in 2026.

A ‘Family Reunion’

Even as ILTACON continues to grow and feature cutting-edge technology, it has still “retained that family reunion type of feel,” Joy says.

This allows conference organizers “to give the ILTA experience to a lot of people in one place.”

There’s a “culture of trust and sharing” on display at ILTACON that isn’t possible in all industries. Joy draws a comparison between legal tech and other industries, recalling a conversation with a CIO from the oil and gas sector.

“Nothing like this exists in other industries,” she remembers the CIO saying. “You would never have Exxon and Shell in the same room talking about things that they’re doing, even though their problems are very much the same.”

ILTACON, by contrast, creates “a giant tent where there are a lot of really great conversations in an environment where people trust each other to have those conversations.” This trust is what Joy says sustains the culture of community — and sets ILTA apart.

Joy says three essential elements make up a successful event from the perspective of an attendee: Answering questions you needed to find the answers to, coming up with questions you never even knew you needed to ask, then asking them, and meeting someone who can help you.

“You should be able to say: ‘Yeah I’m not alone. Other people are having these issues. Other people have solved them, and we have a way to solve them together,’” she says.

‘What’s Next After What’s Next?’

If tech is everywhere in the legal industry, then so is AI. The emergence and development of this technology has been in the spotlight at events like ILTACON for several years now.

At ILTACON this year, the AI conversation will likely be more forward-looking than before.

“Two years ago, it was ‘Should we?’” Joy says. “Last year, it was ‘How do we?’ This year, it’s ‘Look what we’ve done,’ and ‘What’s next?’”

Joy points out that, in the big picture, we are only in the “first nanosecond of AI,” and much more is to come in the near and distant future.

These types of themes will be explored this year with masterclasses in new tech and speakers who are at the forefront of emerging legal technology.

And while AI has so many exciting new developments, Joy notes, there are still many essential legal technologies that don’t involve AI.

“We still have to get people computers and phones, we still have to help them use the tools that we give them,” she says. “It’s not all just about the shiny new toys.”

‘Solving Specific Problems’

While ILTACON favors its traditions, this year also promises a lot of new features.

One is Lessons in Leadership, a publication featuring essays and entries by ILTA members. A new edition will be offered at ILTACON this year, one which Joy laughingly says is “a lot funnier.” This edition will be available in the Author’s Corner, a place where attendees can go to book signings, browse books for sale, and give attendees opportunities to speak with authors.

The new edition boasts many new submissions, which Joy attributes to the success of the first edition. Joy stresses the importance of “short pointed stories” as vessels of communication in what she dubs our “attention economy,” our “attention world.”

“Storytelling is the most powerful way we have to teach,” she says.

There’s also the Startup Hub, where emerging companies can present their products and services to attendees.

This year’s hub will feature more service providers with an “emphasis on solving specific problems,” Joy says.

Her advice for attendees at the Startup Hub?

“People should be looking there for a lot of good thinking about places where AI can be placed for immediate benefit,” she says.

‘The Bigger Picture’

Joy is still surprised by some trends, especially the rate and amount of money infused by private equity into legal technology.

“We knew it was happening, but it’s accelerated,” she says, and this acceleration has “allowed people to bring things to market earlier.”

There are also some things that aren’t being talked about enough, like the regulatory environment. Individual states will increasingly regulate AI use, she says, creating a highly complex environment for organizations that use this technology.

“It’s volatile right now, it’s moving very quickly,” she says. “The U.S. government attempted to preclude states from independently regulating use of AI, and the Senate voted 99-1 to let the states do what they wanted. When has the U.S. Senate voted 99-1 on anything?”

There’s also the necessity for lawyers to become familiar with their clients’ business operations.

“Our lawyers are going to be increasingly working on problems that involve the use of AI in other businesses,” which means “they need to learn enough about the tech to be able to talk about those issues.”

It’s a situation that provides the opportunity for an organization like ILTACON to have far-reaching effects on the industry — particularly the legal industry, which has been a leader on AI adoption.

“Legal has been very early to adopt this technology,” Joy says. “We have such an opportunity to help people see this in the bigger picture.”

Claire Gallagher is an intern at Breaking Media and a student at Susquehanna University studying Journalism & Digital Media and Spanish. Connect on LinkedIn here.

articles.summary:
There may be no better time for law students to focus on health law. As the health care industry continues to grow, so does the need for lawyers who can untangle the increasingly complicated web of regulations, transactions, patient rights, public policy, and compliance concerns that comes with it. On top of all that, with new technology constantly transforming how care is delivered, the legal questions aren’t getting any easier. Fortunately, the law schools excelling in this area are giving students more than a textbook education, offering hands-on experience through medical-legal partnerships, clinics, and public health advocacy. For students looking for a practice area with plenty of complexity, real-world impact, and staying power, health law may be just what the doctor ordered. 

The National Jurist’s preLaw magazine recently released its ranking of the best law schools for health law on its Health Law Honor Roll, highlighting schools for the strength of their programs. Here’s the methodology that was used:

preLaw magazine grades law schools based on the breadth of their curricular offerings. Scores are weighted as follows: 30% for a concentration, 24% for a clinic, 12% for a center, 12% for an externship, 9% for a journal, 8% for a student group, 5% for a certificate and added value for additional offerings.

Without further ado, according to preLaw magazine, these are the law schools that earned A+ grades for their health law programs (listed in alphabetical order):

  • Case Western Reserve U.
  • Cleveland State University
  • DePaul University
  • Georgetown University
  • Georgia State University
  • Indiana McKinney
  • Loyola University Chicago
  • Mississippi Christian University
  • Mitchell Hamline School of Law
  • Northeastern University
  • Saint Louis University
  • Seton Hall University
  • Temple University
  • UC Law SF
  • University of Houston
  • UC Law San Francisco
  • University of Maryland
  • University of Memphis
  • University of Wisconsin

Congratulations to all of the law schools that made the cut for this important ranking.

articles.title: ABA Going To Lose Law School Accreditor Role On Same Day It Surrenders To Trump Administration
articles.content:
美国律师协会（ABA）的法律教育委员会预计将于今天下午正式投票取消法学院的多元化和包容性标准，向保守派长期存在的关于ABA认证程序的抱怨低头。该委员会在5月份已经投票决定废除这一标准。尽管代表大会最初不同意，但8月4日，代表大会投票决定允许委员会单独行动。

作为这一懦弱退步的交换，教育部宣布将剥夺ABA的认证权力。

祝贺所有参与这一方略的人！

教育部在审查ABA的认证标准后表示：“我们的工作人员发现认证机构不符合机构的认证法规和认可标准。由于该过程正在进行中，并涉及多个评审阶段，包括9月由一个独立的双党咨询委员会进行的评审，我们将不会评论细节。”

谁能想到特朗普大学的总策划者会对高等教育认证机构心怀怨恨？

教育部模棱两可的表态源于一个事实：ABA几乎肯定并没有违反任何规定。但本届教育部的立场是，即使暂停的标准可能会阻止一名普通的白人男性进入法学院，也是过于苛刻。因此，在将近一年半的高压逼迫后，教育部决定在ABA最后一次臣服时再踩上一脚。

梅丽莎·哈特（Melissa Hart），认证委员会主席，对她尚未见过的调查结果作出回应：

“尽管很难对我们尚未收到的建议发表评论，但我们期待有机会纠正任何误解并澄清记录。”

祝你们在 Kangaroo 法庭享受愉快时光。

我一向批评ABA的认证角色，但始终认为它过去几年过于宽松。它批准了一整层的垃圾学校，这些学校的律师考试通过率很低，却运行着一场学费骗局，摧毁了一代毕业生的财务前景，他们永远无法偿还债务。更严格的标准也符合我坚信的观点，即律师考试应被彻底废除，并替代为一系列严苛的法学院标准，以确保任何从认证法学院毕业的学生都能胜任律师工作。现在，ABA即将失去其认证权，转而由一群右翼播客组成的小组负责，他们自认为哈佛法学院的教学能力不如一所为共和党捐赠者谋取利益的认证学校。这让我想起了那个猴爪的故事。

即使ABA可以更严格，我们也知道他们设定的基准仍然比其他选择更好。对所有州尝试非ABA进入法律行业路径的35年研究表明——包括学徒制、法律办公室研究、通信课程、未经认证的学校——这些替代方案为候选人产生了明显更差的结果。这并不意味着应该完全拒绝尝试替代路径，但可以引用一句著名的改编名言：ABA是历史上最糟糕的法律教育认证机构，除了我们曾经尝试过的所有其他机构。

这一切都不令人意外。本届政府从一开始就与ABA为敌。他们首先针对ABA的司法甄别角色，然后转向法律教育。上年，几乎毫无用处的联邦贸易委员会（FTC）将高昂的法学院学费归咎于ABA的认证要求，这大概就像将食品价格上涨归咎于不收殓垃圾一样荒谬。如果有任何机构推高了法律教育成本，那正是《美国新闻与世界报道》（U.S. News）三十年来奖励提高成本的学校——通过多年提供奖学金以提高LSAT中值分数，增加行政人员数量以提高人均开支，以及虚构就业数据以支撑就业率。

一些共和党控制的州已经抢先于教育部采取行动。德克萨斯州在1月份将认证权力移交给了本州最高法院。佛罗里达州和俄亥俄州也在进行中。一旦本届政府决定将ABA作为靶子，就设定了激励机制，让每个想要提升自己声誉的州官员都可以摆弄认证权。得克萨斯州的法律学位将不值一个宾馆的单层纸巾，但某些参议员选举可以自豪地声称他们确保每一堂侵权法第一课都以《申命记》开场。如果你想知道这将如何发展，可以考虑佛罗里达州新学院的本科经历。罗恩·德桑蒂斯解雇了所有教育专业人士，并实施了新的标准以符合他的政治目标。开支增加，教育成果却一落千丈。

任何人都不该对本届政府在ABA投降后仍然踢它感到震惊。大律师事务所的投降者也发现，不可能从本届政府那里买来和平。有很多原因可以解释这一点，但最简单的理由是，一旦霸凌者选择目标，掏空他的午餐费就变成了次要的，永无止境的羞辱才是重点。无论具体的怨恨是什么，它都只是一个替身。本届政府没有“胜利”，因为整个目的是向福克斯新闻的观众展示他们仍在锤击指定的靶子。

ABA、大律师事务所、贸易伙伴、出生公民……无论特朗普是否成功，殴打必须继续以维持士气。

祝大家享受特朗普大学法学院！
articles.summary:
The American Bar Association’s legal education council is expected to vote this afternoon to formally scrap the diversity and inclusion standard for law schools, acquiescing on a long-standing conservative complaint about the ABA’s accreditation process. The council already voted to repeal this standard back in May. The House of Delegates declined to concur, but on August 4, the House voted to let the council do it without them.

In return for this cowardly backslide, the Department of Education announced that it’s going to yank the ABA’s accreditation power anyway.

Congratulations to everyone involved in this strategy!

“After reviewing ABA’s accreditation standards, Department staff found the accreditor out of compliance with the agency’s accreditation regulations and recognition standards. We will not comment on details as the process is ongoing and involves multiple stages of review, including by an independent, bipartisan advisory committee in September.”

Who would’ve thought the mastermind of Trump University has it out for higher education accreditors?

The Department’s vagueposting here is a byproduct of the fact that the ABA is almost certainly not out of compliance with jack shit. But this DOE takes the position that even a paused standard that might keep one straight C white man out of law school is a bridge too far. So after a year and a half browbeating the organization into submission, the Department decided to step on the ABA’s final act of prostration anyway.

Melissa Hart, who chairs the accreditation council, responded to a finding she hasn’t seen:

“Although it is difficult to comment on a recommendation we haven’t yet received, we look forward to the opportunity to address any misconceptions and clarify the record.”

Have fun in kangaroo court.

I’ve long criticized the ABA’s accreditation role, but always from the position that it spent years being too permissive. It rubber-stamped a whole tier of toilet schools with garbage bar passage rates running a tuition scam that torched a generation of graduates who never stood a chance of paying off their debts. Stricter standards also play into my firm belief that the bar exam should be nuked from space and replaced by a draconian series of law school standards that guarantee anyone graduating from an accredited law school is ready to practice law. Now the ABA is poised to lose its accreditor role to a panel of right-wing podcasters who have convinced themselves that Harvard Law can’t teach as well as a diploma mill that lines the pockets of a Republican donor. That’ll teach me to play around with that monkey’s paw.

Even if the ABA could have been more strict, we know for a fact that the baseline they did set is still better than the alternative. A 35-year study of every state experiment with non-ABA pathways into the profession — apprenticeships, law office study, correspondence programs, unaccredited schools — found that the alternatives produce dramatically worse outcomes for those candidates. That’s not a reason to wholesale reject experiments with alternative pathways, but, to put a new spin on a famous quote: the ABA is the worst legal education accreditor in history except for all the others we’ve ever tried.

None of this is a surprise. The administration has had it out for the ABA since jump. First they went after the ABA’s judicial vetting role, and then they turned to legal education. The functionally useless FTC spent last year blaming high law school tuition on ABA accreditation requirements, which is roughly like blaming grocery prices on not packing road kill. If any institution inflated the cost of legal education, it was U.S. News spending three decades rewarding schools for running up costs — years of scholarships to buy LSAT medians, administrative bloat to goose per-student spending, and career services fictions to prop up employment numbers.

Some Republican-run states already jumped the line on the Department of Education. Texas moved accreditation authority to its own Supreme Court in January. Florida and Ohio are working on it. Once the administration decided to make the ABA a punching bag, it set the incentive structure so every knuckle-dragging state official looking to bolster their bona fides could take a run at accreditation. A law degree from a Texas school is going to be worth less than a single-ply napkin at a BBQ, but someone’s state senate campaign can brag about making sure every 1L Torts class begins with Deuteronomy. If you’re wondering how this will all play out, consider the undergraduate experience of New College in Florida. Ron DeSantis canned all the education professionals and installed new standards that met his political goals. Spending is up and educational outcomes have gone in the dumpster.

Nor should anyone be shocked that the administration would still kick the ABA after it surrendered. The Biglaw capitulators also learned that there’s no such thing as buying peace from this administration. There are a lot of reasons why this might be true, but the simplest is that once a bully picks a target, taking their lunch money becomes secondary to the unending infliction of humiliation. Whatever the specific grievance is, it’s just a placeholder. There’s no “victory” for the administration, because the whole point is to show the Fox News audience that they’re still hammering their appointed punching bags.

The ABA, Biglaw firms, trading partners, birthright citizens… it doesn’t matter if Trump is successful or not, the beatings must continue to sustain morale.

Enjoy the Trump University College of Law, everybody!
